text:
gitops-bot: :rotating_light: env-parity-checker detected a mismatch between desired git state and cluster for cluster=prod-eu-west-1, namespace=runtime-gpu

alex: seeing OOMs on a couple of model pods and the autoscaler didn't spin up. got the alert and stack traces.

maya: link to metrics?

alex: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/cluster-gpu?orgId=1&from=now-2h&to=now - GPU pod evictions spiked at 09:12 UTC, node utilization hitting 98% on a100 pool.

liam: run the parity diff? what exactly disagrees?

gitops-bot: generated drift report:
```
resource: module.nodepools.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_pool
live: desired_capacity = 6, min_size = 1, max_size = 6
git: desired_capacity = 8, min_size = 2, max_size = 8

resource: kubernetes_node_pool.labels: live labels: [accelerator=nvidia-a100] git labels: [accelerator=nvidia-a100, env=prod-gpu]

resource: helm_release/runtime values: live taints: [gpu:demand=true:NoSchedule] git taints: [gpu:demand=true:NoSchedule, region_affinity=eu-west-1:PreferNoSchedule]
```

rachel: wow, min_size dropped to 1 in the live cluster? that explains the slow scale-up. any idea when that change happened?

alex: kube-audit shows a reconciler patch at 2025-11-02T09:07:12Z from our autoscaler operator, but gitops show recent PR merged 2025-11-01 bumping desired_capacity to 8. looks like terraform apply in prod failed mid-plan and the reconciler rolled back to previous nodepool size.

maya: could be two things: terraform plan/app drift or a webhook/protections that partially applied. can we get the tf state history?

liam: pulling state snapshot from backend... one sec.

liam: confirmed - state file shows min_size=1 from 2025-11-02 09:06:50 UTC. the last successful apply before that was 2025-10-28. there's a failed apply log: timeout on asg update, then a retry that truncated the min_size.

rachel: is the reconciler blocked by policy checks? the helm taint mismatch suggests gate rejected the new region_affinity key.

alex: correct. policy-monitor reported a deny on region_affinity because it's a new annotated taint we haven't approved in policy bundle. we should either approve the policy change or reconcile a safe fallback.

maya: immediate mitigation: bump autoscaler min to 4 so launcher can get pods scheduled while we sort policy. can do via ad-hoc terraform apply with emergency tfvars, or manually scale ASG. which is faster?

liam: manual ASG scale is fastest to restore capacity. I'll scale desired_capacity to 6 now and min to 4.

oncall-bot: user liam executed aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-prod-a100 --desired-capacity 6

alex: after manual scale, new nodes join and pods start pending->running. but we still have taint mismatch so some pods prefer others. schedule logs look better.

maya: medium-term: we need to reconcile gitops such that the git state matches policy expectations. rachel, can you open a PR that removes/renames the region_affinity taint to an approved key, or add it to policy allowlist?

rachel: already opening PR against infra-config: https://git.redwood/infra/infra-config/pulls/321 - moving region_affinity into annotations and adding policy exception. includes terraform bump for nodepool min_size=4 and desired=8.

alex: before merging, let's run a dry-run reconcile and a terraform plan in a sandbox. also add a canary rollout: apply to prod-staging first (prod-shadow) and validate metrics.

liam: running `terraform plan -var=env=prod -target=module.nodepools.gpu_pool` now. plan shows +2 desired capacity and +1 min_size. no resource replacement. attaching plan snippet:
```
  # module.nodepools.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_pool will be updated in-place
  ~ desired_capacity = 6 -> 8
  ~ min_size         = 4 -> 4
```

gitops-bot: dry-run reconcile returned: blocked by policy-check: taint key 'region_affinity' not in allowlist.

maya: approve the policy exception in the PR and run the policy CI so reconcile can proceed. rachel, mark it as emergency if needed.

rachel: PR includes policy change and a note for Security. tagging @security for approval.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-20251102-007 - Prod GPU capacity / env parity drift. assigned to eng-infra oncall.

alex: after security sign-off we should merge and let gitops apply. if gitops still fails, we should fallback to automated reconciler with controlled concurrency: `gitops-sync --force --max-concurrent=2` to avoid partial applies.

liam: security approved in 12 mins. merging PR now.

gitops-bot: merge completed: infra-config@main at commit abc123. starting automated sync to prod-eu-west-1.

gitops-bot: sync step 1/3: applying helm release runtime -> OK

gitops-bot: sync step 2/3: applying terraform changes -> plan OK, apply started

gitops-bot: sync step 3/3: verifying resources -> OK

alex: nodes scaled to desired 8, workloads redistributed, evictions dropped. great.

maya: follow-up actions: 1) add an autoscaler apply timeout guard so partial applies are rolled back safely; 2) add policy CI to detect new taint keys before merge; 3) add alert rule when git vs live desired_capacity delta > 1. I'll file tickets.

rachel: created tickets: INFRA-921 (apply-timeout-guard), INFRA-922 (policy-ci-taint-check), INFRA-923 (parity-delta-alert).

alex: thanks all. closing incident once a full 2h SLA window is green. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: INC-20251102-007 status -> resolved (2025-11-02T11:03:12Z)
